about.title: Tulare Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Tulare's roads carry a steady mix of local traffic and regional travelers moving along SR-99, Blackstone, Bardsley, and Rt 137, and public crash records show dozens of injury collisions here each year, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the most reports. After a crash, the days that follow matter: insurers move fast, evidence can disappear, and California's comparative fault rules mean what you say early on can affect your claim later. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured Tulare residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you pay nothing upfront and nothing at all unless there's a recovery. Before you talk to an insurance adjuster or sign anything, it's worth understanding where you stand. We can help you get that conversation started quickly and without cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file suit, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity is involved — a real possibility on Tulare's public roadways.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Both Ways
items.desc: California lets you recover even if you're partly at fault, but any statement you give the other driver's insurer can be used to shift blame onto you, so it helps to speak with an attorney first.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but insurers still push back hard — an independent attorney working on contingency has an incentive to push just as hard for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Tulare?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your accident involved a government vehicle or road hazard on a city- or county-maintained street, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's smart to act quickly.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements to shift fault under California's comparative fault rules, which can reduce what you're able to recover later.

items.question: Why do so many crashes happen on Fridays in Tulare?
items.answer: Public crash records show Friday afternoons, especially between 3 and 5 p.m., as a peak time for reported injury collisions in Tulare, likely tied to end-of-week traffic on corridors like SR-99 and Bardsley. That doesn't mean any particular road is unsafe — just that traffic volume and driver fatigue tend to rise then.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
